'''Robert John McCann''' {{post-nominals|country=CAN|FRSC}} is a Canadian [[mathematician]], known for his work in [[Transportation theory (mathematics)|transportation theory]]. He has worked as a professor at the [[University of Toronto]] since 1998, and as Canada Research Chair in Mathematics, Economics, and Physics since 2020.

==Life and work==
McCann was raised in [[Windsor, Ontario]]. He studied engineering and physics at [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]] before graduating with a degree in math, and earned a PhD in mathematics from [[Princeton University]] in 1994.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fields.utoronto.ca/people-and-contacts/scientific-advisory-panel#RMcCann|title=Scientific Advisory Panel|website=[[Fields Institute|The Fields Institute for Research in Mathematical Sciences]]|date=24 December 2014 |access-date=3 June 2019}}</ref> McCann was a Tamarkin Assistant Professor at [[Brown University]] from 1994, before joining the [[University of Toronto Department of Mathematics]] in the fall of 1998.<ref>{{cite journal|title=New Faculty Appointments|date=July 2000|journal=Mathematics|publisher=Department of Mathematics, University of Toronto|pages=4–5|url=http://www.math.toronto.edu/dept/newsletters/MATH_NL_00.pdf}}</ref> He served as editor-in-chief of the ''[[Canadian Journal of Mathematics]]'' from 2007 to 2016, and again since 2022.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2017/2017-jw-prize|title=Professor Robert McCann to receive the 2017 CMS Jeffery-Williams Prize|location=Ottawa|publisher=[[Canadian Mathematical Society]]|date=23 February 2017|access-date=3 June 2019|archive-date=4 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190604014930/https://cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2017/2017-jw-prize|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Seoul in 2014.<ref>{{cite book|author=McCann, Robert J.|chapter=Academic wages, singularities, phase transitions and pyramid schemes|title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians (Seoul 2014)|volume=3|pages=835–849|year=2014}}</ref> He was elected a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2012, of the Royal Society of Canada in 2014, of the Fields Institute in 2015 and of the Canadian Mathematical Society in 2020. In 2025 he received the [[Norbert Wiener Prize in Applied Mathematics]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/news?news_id=7381 Norbert Wiener Prize in Applied Mathematics 2025]</ref>
